page_1.thesis_2_heading: An observed premium-mix shift supports the sales ramp
page_1.thesis_2_body: Q3 server ASP rose 54% and units 10% YoY. I underwrite continued premium-product adoption; the selected 2028 sales forecast is $90.01B versus $83.72B consensus.
page_1.recommendation_sentence: The operating thesis is positive; the current quote does not meet my return requirements. Re-underwrite delivery and cash conversion before any purchase at $40 or below.

page_3.replace_counterexample_callout: Holding modeled Q4 ASP flat gives $71.17B of 2027 company sales and $88.32B in 2028, still above consensus. The 10% annual-ASP counterexample implies roughly 6% below that modeled Q4 level; it gives $69.33B and $85.84B. The exit anchor and later growth remain forecasts.
page_3.source_change: Add the new demand calculation artifact to the build provenance; retain Intel Q3 and TrendForce links. The flat-Q4 control and 10% case are distinct assumed paths, not observed outcomes.

page_5.right_section_heading: Why I carry the mix shift forward
right_bullets: Observed mix recovery. Q3 server ASP rose 54% and units 10% YoY. Intel attributes most ASP improvement to premium mix, alongside higher unit costs.

Customer adoption supports persistence. Intel reports signed DCAI long-term agreements, including Google; Google confirms expanded Granite Rapids deployments. Public terms do not establish quantities or net prices.

The forecast carries that transition forward. $5.10B of 2027 CPU growth is modeled exit run-rate carryover; $4.49B is further ramp. The $6.81B Q4 anchor must be verified, and richer mix must reach group cash.
page_5.retain: Left quarterly CPU chart, Q4 allocation explanation, and H1 delivery table.
page_5.footer_addition: Intel Q1 prepared remarks, p.4; Google April 22 compute update. Contracts and deployments support adoption, not disclosed purchase quantities, net prices, or Intel margins.

page_7.right_section_heading: What a $40 entry earns in each case
page_7.table_note: The selected stress retains the faster CPU path. The combined CPU-delay case is jointly recalculated and funded; these are unweighted outcomes, not a downside floor.
page_7.bottom_prose: Require 15% annually in the updated higher-rate core and 12% in the updated selected stress. Rebuild CPU sales, group cash and funding after material news, then recalculate the remaining horizon to December 2030. The November 6 ceiling rounds down to $40; it expires if the operating assumptions no longer hold.
page_7.bottom_callout: The funded combined setback supports a $37.17 diagnostic ceiling for 12%, not an adopted entry recommendation. No rule requires every downside to meet the hurdle.
page_7.move_to_notes: Reverse-cash table and detailed equivalent perpetuity calculation; these already appear in defense page 7.

page_9.heading: Revenue Must Become Parent Cash
page_9.subtitle: Core 2030 recurring cash is $19.45B; the combined setback gives $15.33B
funding_bullets: Capital stays committed. Both cases retain $124.5B of 2027–30 physical capex. Lower sales do not create an immediate capex refund.
Timing requires borrowing. The combined stress draws $2.65B at an assumed 8%, repays in Q4 2028 and incurs $126M of interest. The funded 2030 target is $59.50.
Capacity is disclosed; access is assumed. Intel reports $15B of revolvers, including $5B maturing in 2029. Fees and future covenant compliance are not established by this calculation.
page_9.bottom_heading: The remaining bet is durable cash conversion
page_9.bottom_prose: Core parent cash excluding finite credits stays negative in 2027–28; the positive 2030 cash is forecast. 92.9% of operating value comes after 2030. The 2031–40 model assumes $0.80 of incremental sales per dollar of net investment; R&D remains expensed.
page_9.footer: Sources: Intel Q3 facilities and claims; analyst cash and funded-stress calculations. Combined setback adds the persistent CPU delay to Foundry breakeven, 15% terminal return on modeled net investment from 2041, and the higher rate. Net investment follows the existing model. Credits are finite. Parent cash excludes financing; borrowing creates matching debt.

notes_9_and_10.replace_answer_why_prefer_faster_path: The continuation case has Intel-specific support: reported premium mix, signed DCAI long-term agreements and customer-confirmed deployments. I do not extrapolate the Q3 54% ASP increase. Conditional on the modeled Q4 level, flat ASP still leaves sales above consensus; the 10% annual-ASP counterexample implies a decline from that exit. The uncertainty is persistence and the exact anchor, not whether premium mix has occurred. I will rebase the future level if Q4 disclosures or H1 delivery contradict it.
notes_9_and_10.replace_answer_why_advance_no_purchase: The pitch makes a conditional investment judgment from an observed product transition and a quantified cash path. It identifies the evidence required to retain the forecast, the price that compensates for selected risks, and how that price changes after a setback. I would not buy at $56.28 or raise the target to manufacture upside. The conditional recommendation must compete on this reasoning; it is not a claim of a current-price bargain or a guaranteed winning entry.
notes_9_and_10.update_combined_case_numbers: Use the fully funded combined CPU-delay target of $59.50, annual return at $40 of 10.0%, and diagnostic 12% ceiling of $37.17. Keep the previously calculated pre-financing results labeled as such only if retained for an explicit reconciliation.
